## TL;DR

The round 1 reviewer found no implementation bugs in the Muse usage behavior, dashboard/docs labeling, or needs-input body-update handling. The task was returned to active with one landing blocker: the branch conflicted with current main in `PipelineCard.vue`. I merged main into this branch, preserved the contrast correction, and retained the latest main copy of the task record. The required changed-main check is being rerun before requesting review round 2.

## Work and rationale

I read the full round 1 report before taking action. It confirmed that a null allowance with a reason and hint reaches the user-facing message, a null allowance without those fields gets a fallback, CLI and login failures are represented as an actionable successful response, and normal allowance windows still render as bars. The reviewer also confirmed the Muse docs destination is honestly labelled and that the task body update tests cover the requested flag behavior. No code defect was reported.

The only reported blocker was a merge conflict in `src/ui-app/src/components/PipelineCard.vue`. The conflict was between this task’s change from `--muted` to `--muted-foreground` and main’s parallel change to `--txt-dim` for the same four muted labels. Both tokens are defined in the shared style sheet with the same light and dark theme values. I kept `--muted-foreground`, which is the semantic text token and the exact contrast correction the reviewer had already affirmed. This integrates the main version’s equivalent appearance while keeping the explicit foreground role used by this task.

The merge also reported a conflict in this task’s work record. Per the repository merge rule, I kept main’s copy rather than carrying older status and activity metadata forward. The task’s implementation files and tests remain in the task branch, and the task is active for this revision.

## Approaches tried

I read `work/reports/1067/review-1.md` and its structured record, then checked the task’s live state and landability. `repoos sync 1067` could not proceed while the task’s current agent turn was active. I therefore merged the main ref into this worktree. Git reported conflicts only in the pipeline card and the task’s own work record. I resolved the pipeline styling to the shared semantic foreground token, retained main’s task record, and staged those merge resolutions. The remaining main changes were included by the merge.

## Challenges and blockers

The automatic sync command refused because RepoOS detected an agent turn in progress, so the documented manual merge path was needed. The source conflict involved two equivalent theme tokens rather than two different visual treatments. I verified both declarations in the shared stylesheet before choosing the foreground semantic token. The check result is not yet recorded in this draft; it will be added after the required changed-main check completes.

## Key learnings

The first review validated the behavior and isolated the issue to branch integration. A semantic theme token can coexist with a parallel legacy-token rename when both are backed by the same light and dark values. Keeping the semantic token preserves the contrast fix while integrating the current main tree. The task record is bookkeeping owned by RepoOS, so a merge conflict there should use main’s current copy rather than manually reconciling status history.

## Check follow-up

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the merged tree. Remote validation initially hung on its first host; RepoOS terminated that validation container and retried on a second host. The retry completed the build and scoped tests successfully. Local checks also passed: formatting, lint, build freshness, CSS and theme guards, hardcoded-color scan, rendered contrast, UI smoke, task asset guard, and the user-docs build. The final tree is ready for review round 2.
